scope: Per-request token counts, cache hits, predictions, bounds, parity and engine timings

claims.claim: From the capture alone, the predictor put this trace's eviction threshold at 488 blocks, with exactly 32 tokens lost at 487; vLLM matched both on all 30 requests.
demonstrates: the predictor locates one trace's threshold at the engine's resolution of one block
prompt-ID parity on every replayed request

claims.claim: The free-queue predictor matched vLLM's reported cached tokens on every sequential request on CPU and T4, and on 710 of 738 requests under live concurrency.
claims.engine: vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev595+g2173d7121, Mac CPU (Apple M5) and Tesla T4
demonstrates: exact per-request hit prediction for sequential replay on one vLLM build
the remaining overlap error is small and concentrated in evicting runs
does_not_demonstrate: the cause of the overlap misses, which needs engine-side events
agreement with vLLM's native simulator, which was not run

claims.claim: A baseline that assumes matching blocks stay cached was exact on 256 of 265 concurrent requests with 8,320 tokens of total error, against 259 and 352 for the overlap predictor.
demonstrates: modeling residency accounts for the baseline's error, which equals the evicted reuse
does_not_demonstrate: workloads without eviction, where the two agree

claims.claim: Single sessions reused 95%, 95% and 79% of prompt tokens from turn 1, and new content was 68%, 64% and 91% of what they recomputed.
demonstrates: the split of recomputation by cause for three sessions with no eviction

claims.claim: With thinking off, Qwen3's template drops the 4-token empty thinking cue from history, so every turn that kept its reply diverged inside the cue; serving the cue kept removed the re-prefill but changed the model's next action.
demonstrates: the boundary in every Qwen3 capture and in none of the Qwen2.5 control
does_not_demonstrate: an effect on task success: no session solved the task

claims.claim: smolagents 1.26.0 writes each tool call into history as text of 52 to 66 tokens with a random call ID, for calls generated in 19 to 36 tokens, so its replies cannot be reused.
demonstrates: one harness version's serialization and its effect on reuse

claims.claim: Two of nine concurrent runs evicted, losing 3,680 and 4,640 tokens; the fixed trace lost 12,832 and 4,512 tokens at 384 and 438 blocks and none from 488 up, identically on CPU and T4.
claims.engine: vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev595+g2173d7121, Mac CPU (Apple M5) and Tesla T4
demonstrates: eviction appears only below the trace's working set, as predicted
does_not_demonstrate: the per-run threshold calls (9 of 9), which need the captures; see the repetitions record

claims.claim: On a Tesla T4 the 30 requests took 43.9 s, 30.9 s and 23.6 s of total time to first token at 384, 438 and 488 blocks: 86% and 31% more where blocks were evicted.
demonstrates: the measured cost of eviction for one trace sent one request at a time
does_not_demonstrate: the per-token slope's per-request basis, which was not retained

claims.claim: Replaying one evicting trace with at most two sessions at a time, greedily, or one at a time removed eviction and cut recomputation from 26,363 to 22,011 tokens.
demonstrates: what reordering one fixed trace does to eviction and recomputation
does_not_demonstrate: wall-clock delay, which is counted in positions

claims.claim: Live, a two-session cap removed eviction in every seed, cutting seed 4's wall clock from 1,242.8 s to 299.0 s; the second token-budget version lost 3,456 and 3,616 tokens in seeds 4 and 5.
demonstrates: eviction under each limit, per seed
the waiting a cap adds where nothing would be evicted
does_not_demonstrate: paired comparisons of totals, since sampled trajectories differ
